A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiverseVAR by the same authors. Their complete main texts, references, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments on Infinity and Switti, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds video generation, class-conditioned generation, scalability analyses, and evaluated fine-tuning baselines.

M1.justification: The core condition-annealing and scale-travel algorithm remains unchanged. Limited inference extensions apply it to InfinityStar's keyframe stage and to class-label embeddings, while Appendix F.4 introduces repeated scale-travel execution rather than the original single refinement.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates text-conditioned image generation. V2 additionally evaluates text-to-video generation using VBench-2.0 prompts and class-conditioned generation on ImageNet. Appendix I also introduces LAION training data for the adapted Kaleido comparator. MS-COCO, MJHQ-30K, and existing text-alignment evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Appendix I adds actual comparisons against CSD-VAR and an adapted Kaleido method; CSD-VAR was only cited in v1. The prompt-rewriting comparison also changes membership: v1's Switti comparison disappears, while v2 directly compares Infinity with and without prompt rewriting and DiverseVAR.

E3.justification: New protocols include InfinityStar-8B generation at 480p with 81 frames, VBench diversity and quality metrics, and class-conditioned evaluation using ten images per ImageNet class with FID, precision, and recall. Additional tests vary model size, output resolution, and refinement count. The retained main image experiments keep their original settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of repeated scale-travel, sensitivity to model size and resolution, and a detailed-prompt case study comparing prompt rewriting and its combination with DiverseVAR. Existing scheduler and scale-parameter ablations remain. The CFG sweep is moved into the main text but loses its zero-guidance condition.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly identifies three seed-indexed generations in its video comparisons, whereas v1 only discusses varying random seeds generally. This is limited additional seed reporting: neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-evaluation uncertainty estimates, and existing runtime averaging remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1's image scores are unchanged. New results include video diversity/quality scores of 0.487/0.804 for DiverseVAR versus 0.270/0.806 for InfinityStar, and class-conditioned FID of 5.560 versus 10.578 for VAR. V2 also adds repeated-refinement, scalability, fine-tuning-baseline, and combined prompt-rewriting results. Zero-CFG results, Switti prompt-rewriting results, and several qualitative examples are removed.

T1.justification: The VAR factorization, noise-injection schedules, multi-scale encoding, and scale-travel mathematics are retained. V2 removes the illustrative diffusion time-travel equations while shortening that background analogy; this changes exposition rather than the work's formal assumptions, reasoning, or guarantees. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the claimed applicability from text-conditioned image generation to image and video generation. The introduction explicitly claims the best diversity-quality trade-off in both domains. The central training-free condition-annealing and scale-travel contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 explains why prompt rewriting offers less variation for highly constrained prompts and distinguishes changing the prompt from increasing diversity under a fixed condition. It also interprets repeated refinement as trading computation for quality. The existing limitations of additional inference cost and approximately 6% residual artifacts remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds video and class-conditioning hyperparameters, a detailed training/data-processing recipe for the Kaleido adaptation, model-size/resolution specifications, and a project-page URL. Original image settings and hardware/runtime disclosures remain. However, the relocated sampling-control tables lose v1's explicit statement identifying their evaluation prompt set.

R1.justification: The existing VAR and diffusion-diversity positioning is retained. V2 extends the discussion to autoregressive video work, including VideoPoet, Emu3, and InfinityStar, and positions its training-free approach against fine-tuning alternatives. Kaleido and supporting evaluation/tool references are added; CSD-VAR was already cited.

P1.justification: V2 selectively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and refinement explanation, expands the prompt-rewriting discussion, and promotes sampling-control discussions from the appendix into Section 5.4. The supplement gains a contents page and reorganized subsections, while the overall six-section narrative and much existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column formatting with extensively rearranged displays. Figure 1 is redesigned to include video, new video and prompt-rewriting figures are added, and sampling-control tables move into the main text. Appendix image galleries are substantially reduced, while new experimental tables expand the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's two text-to-image backbones through video and class-conditioned experiments and comparisons with trained diversity methods. Repeated-refinement tests and quantified combinations with prompt rewriting also clarify practical trade-offs. Some controls and examples disappear, and the scalability discussion understates the 8B ImageReward drop from 1.29 to 0.81. Nevertheless, the broader, directly relevant comparative evidence materially improves support for the method's applicability and usefulness.
